rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of madness explains the preceding reference to God’s favor and calls the accusation false.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن هذا كالتفسير لما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s visible excellent morals and actions are incompatible with the bad morals characteristic of madmen.
rows.anchor: الأخلاق الحميدة والأفعال المرضية كانت ظاهرة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His conduct was not affectation: as 38:86 says, he did not pretend, and pretense soon gives way to one’s natural disposition.
rows.anchor: لست متكلفا فيما يظهر لكم من أخلاقي لأن المتكلف لا يدوم أمره طويلا بل يرجع إلى الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command in 6:90 to follow earlier prophets concerns their distinctive noble traits, not imitative knowledge of God or their different laws.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since each earlier prophet excelled in a particular virtue, following them all gave Muhammad the combined virtues dispersed among them and an exceptional rank.
rows.anchor: فلما أمر محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام بأن يقتدي بالكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā conveys mastery: the Prophet stands over and commands these noble traits as a master commands a servant.
rows.anchor: وكلمة على للاستعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Character is a settled psychic disposition that makes beautiful actions easy; performing such actions and the ease of performing them are distinct.
rows.anchor: الخلق ملكة نفسانية يسهل على المتصف بها الإتيان بالأفعال الجميلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good character includes avoiding miserliness, stinginess, and anger; kindness in dealings and speech; avoiding estrangement; lenience in contracts; and generosity toward relatives and in-laws.
rows.anchor: يدخل في حسن الخلق التحرز من الشح والبخل والغضب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly interpreted the phrase as meaning that the Prophet followed a great religion.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال معناه

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A report says God told the Prophet that He had created no religion dearer or more pleasing to Him than Islam, which He chose for the Prophet and his community.
rows.anchor: لم أخلق دينا أحب إلي ولا أرضى عندي من هذا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects equating character with religion: religion perfects the theoretical faculty, while character perfects the practical faculty.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا القول ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that khuluq linguistically means habit, whether in cognition or action.
rows.anchor: الخلق في اللغة هو العادة سواء كان ذلك في إدراك أو في فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that the soul’s effortless readiness for true divine knowledge, and lack of readiness for false beliefs, can also be called character.
rows.anchor: فلما كانت الروح القدسية التي له شديدة الاستعداد للمعارف الإلهية الحقة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: When Saʿīd ibn Hishām asked about the Prophet’s character, ʿĀʾisha pointed him to the Quran; when asked again, she said his character was the Quran and recited 23:1–10.
rows.anchor: فإنه كان خلق النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī takes ʿĀʾisha’s answer to indicate a soul naturally drawn to the unseen and repelled by bodily pleasures and worldly happiness.
rows.anchor: نفسه المقدسة كانت بالطبع منجذبة إلى عالم الغيب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa reports from his father that ʿĀʾisha said no one had better character than the Messenger, who answered anyone from his family or companions, “At your service.”
rows.anchor: روى هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas said he served the Prophet for ten years, and the Prophet never reproached him for an act he did or failed to do.
rows.anchor: خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls the Prophet’s theoretical perfection great in 4:113 and his practical perfection great here; together these encompass the human faculties.
rows.anchor: وصف ما يرجع إلى قوته النظرية بأنه عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms of perfection show that the Prophet’s soul ranked exceptionally high among human souls, nearly like the angels in strength and completeness.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق للإنسان بعد هاتين القوتين شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the Prophet as possessing great character, the passage turns to the promise that he and his opponents will see.
rows.anchor: لما وصفه بأنه على خلق عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After contrasting the disbelievers’ charge of madness with the Prophet’s religious and moral excellence, the sura urges firmness despite his few supporters and their many numbers.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر ما عليه الكفار في أمر الرسول ونسبته إلى الجنون مع الذي أنعم الله به عليه من الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are the chiefs of Mecca, who invited Muhammad to follow his forefathers’ religion; the prohibition incites him to oppose them firmly, and this was among the sura’s earliest revelations.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم دعوه إلى دين آبائه

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth explains idhān as softness, accommodation, and speaking in an accommodating manner.
rows.anchor: الإدهان اللين والمصانعة والمقاربة في الكلام

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says one practices idhān in religion or affairs by betraying them while displaying the opposite of one’s intent.
rows.anchor: داهن الرجل في دينه وداهن في أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed compromise is that Muhammad abandon some of his commitments to please them, and they in turn abandon what displeases him.
rows.anchor: تترك بعض ما أنت عليه مما لا يرضونه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s interpretation: they wished Muhammad would disbelieve so that they would disbelieve.
rows.anchor: لو تكفر فيكفرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is nominative rather than subjunctive after the wish because the syntax shifts to an omitted subject’s predicate: they would then accommodate; compare 72:13.
rows.anchor: ولم ينصب بإضمار أن وهو جواب التمني

rows.speaker: هارون
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports that the reader Hārūn claimed some codices read the verb in the subjunctive, yudhinū.
rows.anchor: وزعم هارون وكان من القراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed prohibition singles out disbelievers whose reprehensible traits go beyond disbelief itself.
rows.anchor: وتلك الصفات هي هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥallāf is someone who swears frequently, whether truthfully or falsely; the description warns against habitual oath-taking.
rows.anchor: الحلاف من كان كثير الحلف في الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against habitual swearing recalls 2:224, which forbids making God an obstacle through one’s oaths.
rows.anchor: ولا تجعلوا الله عرضة لايمانكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives mahīn from mahāna, baseness, and gives either low worth in judgment and discernment or contempt for a liar.
rows.anchor: هو فعيل من المهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent false oaths show ignorance of God’s majesty; attachment to worldly aims makes a person contemptible, while self-respect comes from knowing one’s servitude to God.
rows.anchor: كونه حلافا يدل على أنه لا يعرف عظمة الله تعالى وجلاله

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines hammāz as one who attacks people by speaking ill of them and exposing faults.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يهمز الناس أي يذكرهم بالمكروه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the hammāz twists his cheeks behind people’s backs.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن يلوي شدقيه في أقفية الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī refers to his fuller discussion of the term in 104:1.
rows.anchor: الصفة الثالثة : كونه همازا وهو العياب الطعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A talebearer walks between people carrying gossip in order to corrupt their relations; Rāzī also lists the verb’s forms.
rows.anchor: أي يمشي بالنميمة بين الناس ليفسد بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that he is miserly, with khayr meaning wealth.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أنه بخيل والخير المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that he prevented his family from Islam, the good; the verse was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who threatened ten sons and their associates with withholding support if they followed Muhammad.
rows.anchor: كان له عشرة من البنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person described as Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه أبو جهل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the person described as al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaʿūth.
rows.anchor: الأسود بن عبد يغوث

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the person described as al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq.
rows.anchor: الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil explains muʿtadī as an oppressor who exceeds the right and commits injustice.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه ظلوم يتعدى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī also allows the word to summarize a person who reaches the utmost degree in every reprehensible trait.
rows.anchor: ويمكن حمله على جميع الأخلاق الذميمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athīm is an intensive form denoting someone deeply involved in sin.
rows.anchor: وهو مبالغة في الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanations of ʿutull fall into physical description or moral criticism; the word derives from driving someone roughly and harshly, as in 44:47.
rows.anchor: عتله إذا قاده بعنف وغلظة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās interprets ʿutull as strong and large-bodied.
rows.anchor: يريد قوي ضخم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil describes the person as broad-bellied and sturdy in build.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : واسع البطن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes him as foul in character and mean-spirited.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : الفاحش الخلق

rows.speaker: عبيدة بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayda ibn ʿUmayr calls him a glutton and drinker, and also strong and powerful.
rows.anchor: وقال عبيدة بن عمير : هو الأكول الشروب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains ʿutull as coarse and crude.
rows.anchor: هو الغليظ الجافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moral interpretation describes a person as harsh in dispute, crude, and violent.
rows.anchor: أما الذين حملوه على ذم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ defines zanīm as an outsider attached to a people without belonging to them; Ḥassān’s line uses the word for such an appendage.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : الزنيم هو الدعي الملصق بالقوم وليس منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also evokes a hanging extra part; a sheep’s split ear can hang, dry, and remain like an appendage.
rows.anchor: وزنمت الشاة أيضا إذا شقت أذنها فاسترخت ويبست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one report, al-Walīd was an outsider whom Quraysh claimed as kin eighteen nights after his birth.
rows.anchor: وكان الوليد دعيا في قريش وليس من سنخهم ادعاه بعد ثمان عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says his mother committed adultery and his parentage remained unknown until this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بغت أمه ولم يعرف حتى نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says zanīm is a man known for evil and baseness, as a sheep is known by its dewlap.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي هو الرجل يعرف بالشر واللؤم كما تعرف الشاة بزنمتها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the man had a recognizable dewlap-like mark on his neck.
rows.anchor: روى عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : معنى كونه زنيما

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says he had a mark at the base of his ear like a sheep’s dewlap.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : كان في أصل أذنه مثل زنمة الشاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding faults, ʿutull and zanīm are added as especially severe defects: coarseness hardens the heart, and Rāzī says corrupt seed tends to produce a corrupt child.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن هذين الوصفين وهو كونه عتلا زنيما أشد معايبه لأنه إذا كان جافيا غليظ الطبع قسا قلبه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Rāzī cites a Prophetic report that a child born of adultery, that child’s child, and that child’s grandchild will not enter Paradise; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة السلام : ( لا يدخل الجنة ولد الزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes baʿda dhālika like thumma in 90:17, where it means “then.”
rows.anchor: وقيل : ههنا { بعد ذلك } نظير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan recited ʿutull in the nominative as a form of censure.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( عتل ) رفعا على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the alleged partners are objects of worship whom the disbelievers think will make them equal to believers in reward and escape from punishment; compare 30:40.
rows.anchor: أشياء يعتقدون أنها شركاء الله فيعتقدون أن أولئك الشركاء يجعلونهم في الآخرة مثل المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that they mean people who share their belief that Muslims and criminals will be treated alike; they should produce those supporters if truthful.
rows.anchor: في المعنى أم لهم ناس يشاركونهم في هذا المذهب وهو التسوية بين المسلمين والمجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim fails because it has neither rational nor revealed proof, and no rational people agree with it; it is false from every angle.
rows.anchor: فليس لهم من يوافقهم من العقلاء على هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After disproving their claim, the passage turns to the majesty of the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: شرح بعد ذلك عظمة يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm may be accusative as the time for the preceding challenge to bring partners, attached to an implied udhkur, or followed by an omitted event whose deletion heightens awe.
rows.anchor: يوم منصوب بماذا ؟ فيه ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority place the uncovering on the Day of Resurrection and explain the shin as a figure for hardship and distress.
rows.anchor: الأول : وهو الذي عليه الجمهور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked about the verse, Ibn ʿAbbās advised seeking Arabic poetry when Quranic meaning is unclear, since poetry is the Arabs’ register, and cited a line about war standing on a shin to mean distress.
rows.anchor: روي أنه سئل ابن عباس عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse Ibn ʿAbbās quotes, “war stood on a shin,” uses sāq for severe distress.
rows.anchor: وقامت الحرب بنا على ساق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the phrase means the most severe hour of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وروى مجاهد عنه قال : هو أشد ساعة في القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous verse about a shin being bared likewise uses the phrase for a moment requiring resolve.
rows.anchor: فإن شمرت لك عن ساقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another anonymous couplet, “she bared her shin and plain evil appeared,” uses the shin as a figure for a grave crisis.
rows.anchor: كشفت لكم عن ساقها وبدا من الشر الصراح

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr’s line about war baring its shin witnesses to sāq as a figure for war’s severity.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير : ألا رب سام الطرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous line about a red year baring its shin uses the expression for a year of hardship.
rows.anchor: في سنة قد شمرت عن ساقها حمراء تبرى اللحم عن عراقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous exhortation to tighten one’s resolve as war bares its shin likewise witnesses to the idiom of severity.
rows.anchor: قد شمرت عن ساقها فشدوا وجدت الحرب بكم فجدوا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba traces the idiom to people rolling up their clothes to work hard in a serious matter; hence uncovering the shin figuratively means distress.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أصل هذا أن الرجل إذاوقع في أمر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the idiom’s use for hardship is metaphorical; since decisive proofs establish that God is not a body, the wording must be interpreted figuratively.
rows.anchor: فإذا أقمنا الدلائل القاطعة على أنه تعالى

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf reads the phrase as a metaphor for an affair becoming severe, with no actual uncovering or shin, like calling a miser’s hand tied.
rows.anchor: صاحب ( الكشاف ) أورد هذا التأويل في معرض آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says metaphor without proof would license philosophers to turn gardens and rivers in 2:25 or bowing and prostration in 22:77 into mere figures, undermining revealed law.
rows.anchor: إن جوزنا ذلك انفتحت أبواب تأويلات الفلاسفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the metaphor is allowed only after proof that the literal sense is impossible, Rāzī says this is the standard theologians’ method, not a special discovery of rhetorical science.
rows.anchor: فهذا هو الذي لم يزل كل أحد من المتكلمين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الضرير
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḍarīr takes sāq as the basis or core of a matter, as a tree’s or person’s shin supports it; realities and fundamentals will appear at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قول أبي سعيد الضرير : { يوم يكشف عن ساق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the shin as belonging to Hell, the Throne, or a mighty, awe-inspiring angel; the wording does not identify which.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث : يوم يكشف عن ساق جهنم

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: Anthropomorphists take the shin to be God’s; a report attributed to Ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet says God reveals it after questioning the worshippers, believers prostrate, and hypocrites’ backs become rigid.
rows.anchor: والقول الرابع : وهو اختيار المشبهة ، أنه ساق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects a divine body: bodies are finite and originated, are subject to motion and rest, and are contingent; an indefinite shin also suits an immense hardship better than a known divine limb, while uncovering a shin would not identify God.
rows.anchor: الدلائل دلت على أن كل جسم محدث

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim places the event in worldly life, not Resurrection: perhaps a person’s final day, when prayer is called but belief no longer benefits, or infirmity through old age and illness; he compares 25:22 and 56:83.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي مسلم قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers Abū Muslim’s objection that Resurrection has no legal obligations: the call to prostrate can be rebuke and humiliation rather than a legal duty.
rows.anchor: فجوابه أن ذلك لا يكون على سبيل التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported readings use nūn or tāʾ in the verb, with active or passive construction and the Hour or the situation as subject; the sense is that the situation grows severe, by metaphor.
rows.anchor: بالنون و { * تكشف } بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has ta with ḍamma and shin with kasra, from akshafa, meaning to enter into a state of uncovering; akshaf describes an upturned upper lip.
rows.anchor: بالتاء المضمومة وكسر الشين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to prostrate in the Hereafter is not worship or legal obligation but rebuke for having abandoned prostration in worldly life.
rows.anchor: لا يدعون إلى السجود تعبدا وتكليفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the call, God removes their ability to prostrate and blocks their capacity, heightening regret for neglecting the call when their limbs were sound.
rows.anchor: يسلب عنهم القدرة على السجود

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that specifying inability to the Hereafter proves disbelievers had the ability to believe in worldly life, contrary to those who deny such capacity without actual faith.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : لما خصص عدم الاستطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that, on al-Jubbāʾī’s own view, God’s knowledge that a person will not believe is incompatible with that belief, so worldly capacity is absent too.
rows.anchor: أن علم الله بأنه لا يؤمن مناف لوجود الإيمان والجمع بين المتنافيين محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāshiʿatan absāruhum is a circumstantial phrase linked to their inability to prostrate.
rows.anchor: أما قوله : { خاشعة أبصارهم } فهو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are downcast and humiliation overtakes them because they did not persist in serving their master, like a servant abandoned by his master and shamed among people.
rows.anchor: يعني يلحقهم ذل بسبب أنهم ما كانوا مواظبين على خدمة مولاهم مثل العبد الذي أعرض عنه مولاه

words: وَقَدْ كَانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَالِمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life they were called to prayer by the adhān and iqāma while healthy and able to pray.
rows.anchor: يعني حين كانوا يدعون إلى الصلوات بالأذان والإقامة وكانوا سالمين قادرين على الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage threatens those who stay away from congregational prayer and do not answer the muezzin’s call to join it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا وعيد لمن قعد عن الجماعة ولم يجب المؤذن إلى إقامة الصلاة في الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes ṭāghiya as an event exceeding the limit in severity or force, with the root illustrated by 69:11 and 53:17.
rows.anchor: أن الطاغية هي الواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة والقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that view an omitted noun is understood: some identify the event as an overpowering cry, others as an earthquake or thunderbolt.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : إنها الصيحة المجاوزة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second view, transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, takes ṭāghiya as the verbal noun ṭughyān: they were destroyed for rebellion against God, denial of messengers, and unbelief.
rows.anchor: وهو منقول عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj objects that because the next clause names the punishment as a wind, parallelism requires this clause to name a specific punishment too.
rows.anchor: قاله الزجاج : أنه لما ذكر في الجملة الثانية

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī argues that if ṭāghiya meant the cause of destruction, the wording should say they were destroyed for it, rather than bi-ṭāghiya.
rows.anchor: الذي قاله القاضي : وهو أنه لو كان المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view identifies ṭāghiya with the rebellious faction of Thamūd that plotted to hamstring the she-camel; the people were destroyed through that faction’s ill omen.
rows.anchor: أي بالفرقة التي طغت من جملة ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the single man who killed the camel; the whole people were destroyed because they approved his act, and ṭāghiya is an intensive designation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالطاغية ذلك الرجل الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take fīhā to mean in the paths where the wind blew; others take it to mean during those nights and days.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : أي في تلك الليالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarʿā is the plural of ṣarīʿ.
rows.anchor: { صرعى } جمع صريع .

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil explains that they were dead, felled by death.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : يعني موتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāqiya has three explanations: a remnant, a surviving person, or survival itself, with the last like ṭāghiya meaning rebellion.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : في الباقية ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some understand the verse to mean that no descendant of those peoples remained.
rows.anchor: ذهب قوم إلى أن المراد أنه لم يبق من نسل أولئك القوم أحد

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that they lived through seven nights and eight days of the wind’s torment, died on the eighth evening, and were carried by the wind into the sea; this explains 69:8 and 46:25.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج : كانوا سبع ليال
